basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Appellavitque lucem diem et tenebras noctem. Hoc ad intellectum nostrum dictum est; qua'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Appellavitque lucem diem et tenebras noctem. Hoc ad intellectum nostrum dictum est; qua enim lingua appellavit Deus lucem diem ac tenebras noctem; utrum Hebraea, an Graeca, an alia aliqua! Et sic omnia quae vocavit quaeri potest qua lingua vocaverit; sed apud Deum purus intellectus est sine strepitu et diversitate linguarum. Appellavit autem dictum est: Appellari fecit, quia sic distinxit omnia et ordinavit, ut et dies cerni possent, et nomina accipere. Sic enim dicimus: Ille paterfamilias aedificavit istam domum, id est aedificari fecit, et multa talia per omnes libros divinarum Scripturarum inveniuntur.
